newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures erode to mostly lower close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures erode to mostly lower close.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures eroded Monday as the market contemplated a flurry of remarks, mainly from German officials, that focused on interest rates, jobless rates and the European monetary union timetable.

Brokers said many players still favored the long side of the dollar, particularly after a stronger than expected February U.S. national purchasing management index pumped up anxiety about the potential for a rise in U.S. interest rates.
The NAPM rose to 53.1 against forecasts for 52.9. Prices, production, new orders and supplier deliveries all rose, although employment and inventories slipped.

The report also stoked anxiety over whether Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will depart from last week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony when he appears Wednesday before the House Banking Committee.
Traders also waited for this week's reports on German and U.S. employment, with German joblessness widely expected to increase while the U.S. labor market is seen staying tight.
A German newspaper Sunday said unemployment in Germany jumped in February to 4.8 million and a 12.5 percent rate.
But German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Monday he expected unemployment to show only a slight rise in February.
The Federation of German Trade Unions' deputy president said she expected only a slight change in the figures.
Brokers noted that any further deterioration in German employment could make it increasingly difficult for Germany to meet the Maastricht EMU convergence criteria.
Traders said a variety of remarks by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke briefly buffeted the market as well.

He said the mark's depreciation should not continue and the prospect of a U.S. rate hike had narrowed the scope for the Bundesbank to cut rates, He also said the German unemployment situation did not favor a German rate increase.
Yet more talk surfaced that EMU convergence could hit a timetable delay, with muted effect from comments intended to knock down that speculation.
Mexican peso fell on fears objections will grow in Congress to Mexico's recertification as a U.S. drug war ally.
The close in March marks below the $0.5900 area also meant more selling was expected near-term, some brokers added.

March yen fell $0.000081 to $0.008262, marks lost $0.0032 to $0.5894, Swiss lost $0.0007 to $0.6776, pound fell $0.0116 to $1.6176, Can dollar flat at $0.7319, Aus dollar rose $0.0089 to $0.7872, peso fell $0.001100 to $0.124100. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
